p: snared with the words of thy: He forbids us not to become surety one for another, according to the rule of charity, but that we consider for whom and after what sort, so that the creditor may not be defrauded.
ant: If the word of God cannot instruct you, learn from the little ant to labour for yourself and not to burden others.
a little folding of the hands: He expresses the nature of the sluggards, who though they sleep long, yet never have enough, but always seek opportunity for more.
travelleth: That is, suddenly, and when you do not look for it.
an armed man: It will come in such sort, as you are not able to resist it.
a wicked man: He shows to what inconvenience the idle persons and sluggards come, by calling them unthrifty, or the men of Belial, and slanderous.
teacheth with his fingers: Thus all his gesture tends to wickedness,
feet that be swift in running: Meaning, the raging affections, which carry a man away in such sort that he cannot tell what he does.
commandment is a lamp: By the commandment, he means the word of God; and by the instruction, the preaching and declaration of the same, which is committed to the Church.
reproofs of instruction are the way: And reprehensions when the word is preached bring us to life.
eyelids: With her wanton looks and gesture.
Can a man take fire in: Meaning, that she will never cease till she has brought you to begging, and then seek your destruction.
despise a thief: He does not reprove theft, showing that it is not as abominable as whoredom, for theft can be restored, but adultery is permanent, and death by the law of God.
soul when he is hungry: Meaning, for necessity.
wound and dishonour shall he get: That is, death appointed by the Law.

spare in the day of vengeance: He shows that man by nature seeks the death of he that has abused his wife, and so concludes that neither God's law nor the law of nature admits any ransom for the adultery.
